text:
alex: Heads up — we need a quick sync on the new per-route SLO dashboards. Goal: P50/P95/P99 latency, TTFT (first-byte), and tokens/sec. How do we wire runtime -> metrics ingest so console teams can build panels without guessing labels?

maria: +1. Do we have a proposed schema for labels? route_id, model, deployment_group, region, tenant_id (opt). Sampling decisions too — we can't emit every token for high-throughput routes.

sam: For labels I'd say: `route`, `model`, `route_version`, `pool` (dedicated vs hosted), and `fallback` boolean. Keep `tenant_id` out of default high-cardinality streams but allow by opt-in.

ryan: Important: quotas and rate limits modify observed tokens/sec. Console needs to know whether a low tokens/sec is due to throttling vs real traffic drop. Can runtime emit `throttled=true` counter or a `quota_applied` metric?

laura: From the console side we want consistent panel queries. If `throttled` exists we can show a stacked area: user tokens vs throttled tokens. Also want TTFT broken down by `warm/cold cache` tag. How expensive is adding that in runtime?

alex: Runtime note: we already have a short, per-request proto with latency fields. Adding a few labels is cheap but high-cardinality labels (tenant_id, full prompt_hash) will blow metrics. We can emit high-cardinality to a separate, sampled stream.

maria: Proposal: two exports from runtime: 1) high-volume aggregated stats per 1s bin with limited label set (route, model, pool, region) including p50/p95/p99 via HDR histograms; 2) sampled request traces (1/1000 default) with expanded labels + full TTFT. That lets console panels use aggregates and debug workflows use traces.

sam: Sounds good. For histograms we'll expose Prom-style metrics: `redwood_route_latency_seconds_bucket{route=...,model=...,pool=...,region=...}` and a gauge `redwood_route_ttft_seconds{quantile=\"0.5\",...}` or use the histogram quantiles derived in the metrics backend? Need to pick one to avoid double-processing.

ryan: Can we also add a `redwood_tokens_rate_per_sec{route=...,model=...}` counter delta exported as a gauge to show tokens/sec? If we emit counters with labels same as latency aggregates, console can compute rates.

laura: Console wants: default dashboard templates that accept a `route` variable and show: P50/P95/P99 latency, TTFT (p50/p95), tokens/sec 1m/5m, and throttled fraction. Also a small panel for request count and error rate. If sam/maria can lock label names, I can build templates.

alex: Agree on label names: `route`, `model`, `pool`, `region`. Optional `tenant_id` must be flagged as `sensitive_label=true` in config and routed to sampled stream only. We'll add `throttled` as a counter `redwood_throttled_requests_total{route=...,model=...}`.

maria: Implementation detail: runtime will emit HDR histograms to internal metrics proxy over gRPC. Proxy will roll up per-second buckets and publish to metrics backend (Prom/TSDB) as normalized histograms. We'll include the `ttft_ms` histogram too.

sam: UX for rollouts: when we introduce new label `pool`, older dashboards need graceful fallback. Add a migration plan: 2 weeks dual-writing (legacy label set + new label set) then switch console templates to new labels.

ryan: Who owns the sampling config? infra? runtime? We should centralize sampling rates per route in the platform so SRE/product can tweak without deploys.

alex: Ownership: runtime emits, infra (telemetry team) owns the ingest proxy and sampling enforcement, console owns dashboards, eng-platform owns label schema contract. Let's put that in a tiny ownership doc and share.

laura: I'll prototype a dashboard using mocked data if you give me the exact metric names and a sample PromQL for p95 and tokens/sec.

sam: Example PromQLs (rough):
```
# p95 latency from histogram
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_route_latency_seconds_bucket{route=~\"$route\"}[5m])) by (le, route, model, pool, region))
# tokens/sec
sum(rate(redwood_tokens_processed_total{route=~\"$route\"}[1m])) by (route, model, pool, region)
# throttled fraction
sum(rate(redwood_throttled_requests_total{route=~\"$route\"}[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(redwood_requests_total{route=~\"$route\"}[5m])) by (route)
```

maria: Nice. For TTFT p50 we should use the `ttft_histogram` and `histogram_quantile(0.5, ...)`. Confirm that the ingest proxy preserves histogram buckets.

alex: Yes, proxy will preserve HDR buckets. We'll run a short experiment on one low-traffic route next week to validate cardinaility + cost.

ryan: Ops question: alerting. We want synthetic alerts on route-level p99 > X ms and tokens/sec drop > 70% for >5m. Will console own alerts or SRE?

laura: Console will ship panel templates + suggested alert queries; SRE must sign off and add them to global alerting.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: telemetry-proxy v0.9.1 deployed to staging at 2024-03-18T15:12:30Z :rocket:

alex: OK next steps: (1) eng-platform PR with label schema + migration plan (sam/maria) by EOD Thu, (2) telemetry team to add sampled stream + `throttled` metric in staging this sprint (ryan), (3) console to build template with mocked data (laura). I'll put a short OWNERSHIP note in the design doc.

maria: I'll draft the config flags for sensitive label opt-in and sampling rates.

sam: I'll start the PR and include example PromQLs + dashboard variables.

laura: I'll mock the panels and share screenshot in #eng-platform when ready. :eyes:

alex: Thanks all. If anyone runs into cost/cardinality surprises ping me.
